ASH Refactoring: Move CrOS app dialog strings to ash_strings.grd

Fifteen ChromeOS-only app uninstall, pause, and block dialog strings
previously lived in chrome/app/generated_resources.grd even though
they were referenced only from
chrome/browser/ui/views/apps/app_dialog/.

Move these strings and their screenshot hashes to ash/ash_strings.grd
in their original order, update BUILD.gn and DEPS, and remove unused
generated_resources references.

Fix and re-enable BrowserFrameViewBrowserTest.SaveCardIcon

The save card page action (kActionShowPaymentsBubbleOrPage) was missing
from AppBrowserController::GetTitleBarPageActions(), so web app windows
never created a page action view for it. The legacy, now-unused
GetTitleBarPageActionTypes() still lists PageActionIconType::kSaveCard,
so this restores parity with the old behavior.

Web app windows always use the Views-based WebAppFrameToolbarView, even
when WebUILocationBar is enabled, so the test no longer skips the
BrowserFrameView containment check in WebUI mode.

The test also waited ~30s for an Autofill server prediction query that
never resolves in tests. Add AutofillBrowserTestEnvironment, which
disables Autofill server communication for browser tests, to remove the
hang and the flakiness it caused.

[OSCrypt] Expose active encryption provider on Encryptor

Enterprise reporting and Device Trust on Windows need to check whether
Chrome is actively encrypting data with App-Bound Encryption ("v20")
rather than falling back to DPAPI ("v10"). Because
`Encryptor::IsEncryptionAvailable()` returns true whenever any key
provider is active, callers cannot tell them apart without a dummy
`EncryptString()` call.

Add `Encryptor::provider_for_encryption()` (`encryptor.h`) so callers
can inspect the active encryption provider tag directly, and promote
`//chrome/elevation_service:public_headers` to `public_deps` on
`//chrome/browser/os_crypt:app_bound_api` for consumers of
`app_bound_encryption_win.h`. Used by https://crrev.com/c/8680162 and
https://crrev.com/c/8680861.

Bug: 441040062
Test: components_unittests --gtest_filter=EncryptorTest.*
Test: components_unittests --gtest_filter=OSCryptAsyncTest.*

5329ad2311de03d68cfc4fa1c649024b7e8b2dd9 [ diff ] 
Notify view transitions before commit snapshot

View transitions can throttle an `iframe` from `WillCommit`. Canceling
its active compositor animations there can wait for commit completion,
triggering `CHECK(!inside_will_commit_)`.

This change moves view-transition commit observation to
`WillSnapshotCommitState, immediately before the outgoing commit state
is snapshotted. This keeps throttling and animation cancellation
synchronous while leaving other `WillCommit` processing and its
protected-state guard unchanged.

It also adds a WPT that validates the behavior in this scenario,
crashing without this fix.

Fixed: 583171173, 583122300, 584585294

[3p freshness] apr: Update to 1.7.6

Roll third_party/apache-portable-runtime/src from 1.5.2 (2015) to 1.7.6
(2025-05-16), the latest release.

Regenerate include/apr.h and include/arch/unix/apr_private.h: run
./configure from the 1.7.6 release tarball on Linux, as for 1.5.2, then
apply the Android edits with the new apply_android_edits.py. The script
applies the edits that diff.patch used to carry, plus a few for code and
checks that are new since 1.5.2:
- HAVE_DECL_SYS_SIGLIST: bionic declares sys_siglist, newer glibc does
  not, so configure on Linux no longer detects it.
- getrandom() needs API level 28 (Cronet's minimum is 24), so keep
  reading /dev/urandom as before.
- No shm_open() in bionic and no SysV semaphores (semtimedop() needs API
  level 26).

1.5.2's change of apr_int64_t from long to long long is no longer needed:
apr.h now uses int64_t.

BUILD.gn: add the new Unix sources for 64-bit atomics and pollset
wakeup. Like encoding/apr_escape.c before, the new optional APIs
(apr_encode, apr_cstr) are not built because nothing uses them.

include/DEPS: apr_private.h now includes "arch/apr_private_common.h"
(found through src/include), which checkdeps needs to allow.

README.chromium: version, and how to regenerate the headers.

Built //third_party/netty-tcnative:netty-tcnative-so for Cronet Android
arm and arm64 (min SDK 24). The only new libc symbol it needs is
if_indextoname(), available at all API levels.

[3p freshness] apr: Use a pristine upstream checkout in src/

third_party/apache-portable-runtime/src pointed to
chromium/external/apache-portable-runtime, a Chromium-made repository:
the APR 1.5.2 release tarball after running ./configure, with
diff.patch applied and a later NDK r16 fix. It cannot be rolled
automatically.

Switch src/ to the mirror of the upstream Git repository,
https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/github.com/apache/apr, at the
same release, tag 1.5.2. Its sources are identical to the old copy.
The only build inputs that are not in upstream's repository are the two
headers that ./configure generates, include/apr.h and
include/arch/unix/apr_private.h. Check them in outside src/, unchanged
from the old copy (configure output plus the Android edits), and put
them on the include path ahead of src/:

- BUILD.gn: add include/ and include/arch/unix, and export the public
  include dirs through apr_config, so netty-tcnative no longer
  hardcodes src/include.
- Remove diff.patch; README.chromium now describes the edits.
- README.chromium: URL, Revision, and the Local Modifications.

The DEPS files that the old copy had under src/include/arch/ are not
needed: checkdeps does not look into submodules.

No behavior change: for Cronet Android arm64 and arm,
libnetty-tcnative.so and all apr and netty-tcnative object files are
byte-identical before and after this change.

[3p freshness] brotli: Move upstream code into src/

Move the upstream files into src/, mirroring the upstream repository
layout: c/{common,dec,enc,fuzz,include,tools} -> src/c/..., and LICENSE
and README.md -> src/. Chromium glue (BUILD.gn, DEPS, OWNERS,
DIR_METADATA, README.chromium) stays outside src/. This prepares the
dependency for a Crowbar workflow.

The upstream files are unchanged (renames only). Also:
- BUILD.gn: update source paths and the include directory.
- Update the callers that include headers by full path.
- DEPS: skip src/ instead of dec/ and enc/, and delete the
  Chromium-added fuzz/DEPS and tools/DEPS, so that src/ only holds
  upstream files. Their rules were not needed: fuzz/ and tools/ include
  brotli headers with <> or relative paths.
- README.chromium: License File and the Local Modifications paths.
- inclusive_language_presubmit_exempt_dirs.txt: new enc/ path.
- Add the temporary include/brotli/decode.h shim (see below).

PDFium includes third_party/brotli/include/brotli/decode.h by path, so
add a temporary forwarding header at that path. PDFium will switch to
the src/ path together with a brotli DEPS roll, and the shim is removed
after that reaches Chromium. Because the shim takes the old path, git
shows include/brotli/decode.h as rewritten and src/c/include/brotli/
decode.h as added; the added file is the old one unchanged (same blob,
`git diff -M -B` shows the rename).

[webcodecs] Fix AudioEncoder and VideoEncoder reconfigure and error bugs

- Centralize encodeQueueSize decrement, dequeue scheduling, and input
  closing in EncoderBase::ProcessRequests(), block request processing
  while QueueHandleError() is pending, and check reset_count_ in
  HandleError().
- Flush and recreate media::AudioEncoder on configure() instead of
  no-op reconfiguring, and fix active_encodes_ underflow on error.
- Fix premature EndTracing(), stale callback state/reset_count_ checks,
  and getAllFrameBuffers() state checks in VideoEncoder.

Reland "Scope SharedWorkerConnectorImpl lifetime to DocumentService"

This is a reland of commit 7c0bfdd41b8e3570cfce347b1a258460a7ce4701

The original CL was reverted because
WorkerTest.SharedWorkerInPagehideDuringCrossOriginCommit failed on
linux-oi-rel, which runs content_browsertests with
`--enable-features=OriginKeyedProcessesByDefault`. Under
OriginKeyedProcessesByDefault, `https://a.test` and `https://sub.a.test`
are placed in separate origin-keyed SiteInstances unless they opt out of
Origin-Agent-Cluster, causing the initial empty document navigation to
swap RenderFrameHostImpl instead of reusing it in-place.

Patchset 1 is the unmodified original CL. Patchset 2 serves `a.test` and
`sub.a.test` with `Origin-Agent-Cluster: ?0` in the test so they share a
site-keyed SiteInstance and exercise the in-place RenderFrameHostImpl
cross-origin commit under both default and OriginKeyedProcessesByDefault
configurations.

Original change's description:
> Scope SharedWorkerConnectorImpl lifetime to DocumentService
>
> SharedWorkerConnectorImpl was previously owned via
> mojo::MakeSelfOwnedReceiver and stored a GlobalRenderFrameHostId.
> Because its lifetime was tied to the Mojo pipe rather than the
> document lifecycle, Connect() requests sent during document teardown
> could be processed after a cross-document navigation committed in the
> same RenderFrameHost, resolving state against the newly committed
> document.
>
> Convert SharedWorkerConnectorImpl to inherit from
> content::DocumentService so the receiver is closed and destroyed when
> the originating document navigates away. Also track the bound Document
> in Blink's SharedWorkerClientHolder so connector pipes reconnect when
> LocalDOMWindow is reused across same-origin initial empty document
> navigations.
>

[apple] Avoid quadratic bytes concatenation in linker_driver TOC

In LinkerDriver._extract_toc(), accumulating lines into a `bytes` object
with `+=` reallocates and copies the entire buffer on each iteration,
making TOC extraction O(N^2) in the number of exported symbols.

Collect TOC lines in a list and join them once with `b''.join(toc)` so
TOC extraction runs in linear time. Also add unit tests and a presubmit
hook for `build/toolchain/apple/linker_driver_test.py`.

[Content] Flush DeclarativePerformanceObserver on post-header aborts

When a primary main-frame navigation is aborted after receiving
non-redirect HTTP response headers (`OnResponseStarted`) and before
committing a document (`DidCommitNavigation`), no
`DeclarativePerformanceObserver` is instantiated on a
`RenderFrameHost`, so the session report is lost even though the
response carried valid `Performance-Observer` and
`Reporting-Endpoints` headers.

Snapshot the canonical commit origin via `GetOriginToCommit()` at
`NavigationRequest::WillProcessResponse()` when a non-activation
primary main-frame response carries an active
`DeclarativePerformanceObserver` policy and commits a cryptographic
non-opaque origin (`GURL::SchemeIsCryptographic(origin->scheme())`,
matching `RenderFrameHostImpl`'s `SetDocumentReportingEndpoints()`
gate and rejecting 204/downloads and all opaque origins). When such a
navigation is aborted in `WILL_PROCESS_RESPONSE` or `READY_TO_COMMIT`,
call `FlushAbortedPostHeaderNavigation()` on
`DeclarativePerformanceObserver`:
- Build the `navigation`, `visibility-state`, and `session-end` entries
  regardless of `capture-early-failures` and without writing to
  `DeclarativePerformanceObserverStore`.
- Configure a transient `reporting_source` via
  `SetDocumentReportingEndpoints()` with
  `IsolationInfo::CreateForInternalRequest()`, queue the
  `performance-observer` report, and immediately dispatch and expire
  the source via `SendReportsAndRemoveSource()`.

[Offline Pages] Scope offline request headers to their intended load

Offline page NET_ERROR reloads and X-Chrome-offline request headers must
stay scoped to the single local offline page lookup they initiate.
Previously, committing an error page deleted the tab's saved last_n
snapshot before the NET_ERROR reload could serve it, and the reload
omitted an explicit offline ID so lookup fell back to URL matching. When
interception fell back to the network or followed redirects,
X-Chrome-offline remained on the request, exposing the internal header
over the wire and allowing a redirect while online to serve an offline
archive for the redirect target.

Preserve the tab's last_n snapshot across error-page commits (while
fixing the NET_ERROR reload guard so an unservable snapshot cannot
trigger a reload loop), bind NET_ERROR reloads to the matched offline
page ID (failing closed on invalid IDs), and strip X-Chrome-offline at
every redirect and network-dispatch boundary so it never leaves the
browser or re-triggers offline interception on a subsequent hop.

[Offline Pages] Harden redirect URL matching and background auto-fetch

Unify fragment-insensitive URL matching and HTTP/HTTPS scheme validation
between candidate lookup (PageCriteria) and archive serving
(OfflinePageRequestHandler) behind ClassifyOfflinePageUrlMatch() so both
paths enforce OfflinePageModel::CanSaveURL() and share a single contract
that cannot serve an archive under its pre-redirect origin or select
non-HTTP/HTTPS rows.

As defense in depth, also restrict background auto-fetch saves
(auto_async_loading) in BackgroundLoaderOffliner so hidden background
loads cannot follow cross-site redirects or HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrades to
snapshot authenticated cross-site pages. Same-site HTTP-to-HTTPS
upgrades and user-initiated offline downloads remain allowed.

[speech] Allow /proc/cpuinfo in the Linux speech sandbox

XNNPACK, used by SODA when SodaXnnpackDelegate is enabled, needs
/proc/cpuinfo to initialize on x86 Linux. The speech sandbox blocks it,
so every Linux client in the experiment falls back to the built-in TFLite kernels.

[webium] Serve colors.css in process when unbound

Design: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lzWRQwj2u4QItO-Wd3BbhoJbvc7dIxLFBpZeGumxEmw

This CL serves `chrome://theme/colors.css` to an unbound prerendered
toolbar from its local resource loader config, as bound toolbars
already get it, gated behind `TopChromeWebUIPrerenderingUnbound`.

Without this CL, an unbound spare has no user profile when its render
frame is created, so its `colors.css` request goes to `ThemeSource` on
the browser UI thread. At startup, with
`TopChromeWebUIPrerenderingAtStartup`, that request waits behind
startup work and delays the toolbar's first frame.

The spare's color provider is already seeded from the template
profile, so the toolbar generates the CSS from it through
`ThemeColorsSourceManager`'s color provider overload, now public and
static. When the adopting window's colors differ, the bind message
already carries the new `colorsCss`.

Bug: b:573441656
Test: out/Default/unit_tests --gtest_filter='WebUIToolbarUI*:ThemeColorsSourceManager*'
Test: out/Default/browser_tests --gtest_filter='InitialWebUI*:WebUIToolbarUI*:WebUiToolbarJsTest.*'

[media] Let DemuxerManager fall back from SymphoniaDemuxer

With kSymphoniaDemuxing on, DemuxerManager always uses SymphoniaDemuxer
for progressive playback. There is no way to hand media that Symphonia
can't play to FFmpegDemuxer, like DemuxerManager already does for HLS.

Add DEMUXER_ERROR_SYMPHONIA_UNSUPPORTED. When a pipeline reports it,
DemuxerManager stops the pipeline, frees only the demuxer, and asks the
client to restart with FFmpegDemuxer on the same DataSource. If fallback
is disallowed, it stops the DataSource and reports the error. The HLS
and Symphonia paths now share one client restart method,
RestartForDemuxerChange(bool is_hls). Nothing reports the new status
yet. A follow-up has SymphoniaDemuxer report it.

[ChromeVox] Stop Tenji switching to kantenji and showing stale braille

ChromeVox refreshes the braille translator on each focus change. With 6
dot Tenji selected, the display could switch to the 8 dot kantenji table
or show text for an earlier focus.

This happened because the refresh alternated between Tenji and kantenji,
and older async translations could finish last.

To prevent that:
- Keep Tenji selected when no braille table is set.
- Ignore out-of-date refreshes and translations.
- Turn braille off with an announcement if Tenji fails to load.

AX-Relnotes: Fix Japanese braille sometimes showing kantenji or stale text.

Add cache TasksStore and LaunchpadTask struct

Introduces LaunchpadTask to represent tasks generated from sources such
as Gmail and Chrome history, along with TasksStore, an in-memory task
store backed by base::LRUCache (sized by kMaxTasksCacheSize) that
supports adding, clearing, and retrieving tasks.

follow-up CL) and unit tests covering the store functionality.

An unregistered CloudPolicyClient reports NotRegistered to the uploader,

[Policy] Support PolicyRefreshRate on Android

CloudPolicyRefreshScheduler, the local_state policy.user_refresh_rate
pref, and the cloud policy managers are already active on Android, but
the kPolicyRefreshRate mapping sat inside the !BUILDFLAG(IS_ANDROID)
block of kSimplePolicyMap. Move the mapping to the cross-platform table,

iOS use, and set per_profile to false because the pref is registered
only in local_state.

[NTP] Allow mojo_browser_proxy.js in the Microsoft auth frame's CSP

Since crrev.com/c/7851160, the mojom-webui.js files generated for mojom
modules with a *Factory interface import
//resources/mojo/mojo_browser_proxy.js. The bindings for
chrome-untrusted://ntp-microsoft-auth are such a module, and the frame
lists each script it may load in its script-src, which doesn't include
the new module. The frame's scripts then fail to load, the frame never
connects to the New Tab Page, and the Microsoft modules can't sign in.

This CL adds the module to script-src with a comment on what the list
must contain, and adds a browser test that enables the Outlook module by
policy, loads chrome://new-tab-page and waits until the embedded frame
connects to the page. The existing
NewTabPageModulesInteractiveMicrosoftAuthUiTest.LoadMicrosoftAuthIframe
only checks that the <iframe> element exists, so it didn't catch this.

Stop creating multiple PrefetchServices in tests

By merging `PrefetchService`/`TestPrefetchService` members owned by
the test fixture and merge them to
`BrowserContextImpl::prefetch_service_`, to make
`BrowserContextImpl::prefetch_service_` the unique
`PrefetchService` for the `BrowserContext`.

When tests create its `TestPrefetchService`, we store it in
`BrowserContextImpl::prefetch_service_`, by using
`BrowserContextImpl::SetPrefetchServiceForTesting()` and
`BrowserContextImpl::GetPrefetchService()`.

`PrefetchService`s in tests are now destroyed together with the
`BrowserContext`, like in production.

This CL removes the now-unused
`PrefetchDocumentManager::SetPrefetchServiceForTesting()`.

Offset adjusts focus ring's (auto outline) outer stroke radius

The outer corner radii of focus rings are currently set to the same
value as the inner corner radii, without accounting for the offset
between the two strokes. As a result, the outer stroke can appear
thicker around the corners, and a small gap can appear between
the inner and outer strokes.

This CL adjusts the outer corner radii to account for the offset from
the inner stroke, but only when the inner radius exceeds the default
minimum radius to prevent an element with no radius from spilling
at the corners.

This CL also includes:
- Gradually add the default inset for borders thinner than 1px to
  make the transition continuous.
- Allow the default radius to scale down for EffectiveZoom
  less than 1 to avoid the element's concave corners from spilling.

The change is guarded by an enabled-by-default runtime feature flag.

[webium] Keep an unbound toolbar unpainted until it is bound

Design: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1lzWRQwj2u4QItO-Wd3BbhoJbvc7dIxLFBpZeGumxEmw

This CL keeps a prerendered toolbar transparent and inert until it
shows the adopting window's profile, gated behind the
`TopChromeWebUIPrerenderingUnbound` param.

In that mode, one spare toolbar serves windows of every profile. It
loads with a template profile's theme and buttons, and the adopting
window's state arrives later in a bind message.

Today, only message ordering keeps the template profile's state out of
the adopted toolbar's first frame. A late bind message shows another
profile's theme for a frame. With this CL, the worst case is one blank
frame.

How the gate works:

- A page that loads unbound sets `awaiting-bind` and `inert` on
  `toolbar-app`, making it transparent and non-interactive while layout
  still runs.
- `applyBoundProfile()` applies the bind message, then clears
  `awaiting-bind` and `inert`.
- The browser sends a bind message on every adoption, even when no
  field differs, so a template profile window does not stay blank.
- A spare bound before its page commits loads with the window's state,
  skips the gate, and ignores any commit-time bind message.
- `TakeToolbarContents()` CHECKs that the spare is bound to the
  window's profile, since any bind message lifts the gate.

The browser tests check that every frame before the gate lifts is
transparent and inert, and that the first visible frame shows the
window's profile. They cover:

- An Incognito window.
- A second regular profile with a dark theme and the home button.
- A template profile window, whose bind message has no fields.
- A negative control that removes the gate by hand, which shows the
  template profile's state and proves the tests catch it.
- The startup window, whose toolbar ends up ungated.

Ash: Migrate AcceleratorControllerTest off RunUntilIdle, part 1

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to modernize Ash tests by
migrating them away from RunUntilIdle() and toward targeted
synchronization with APIs such as RunUntil(), TestFuture, RunLoop
callbacks, observer waiters, or exact mock-time advancement.

Accepting or cancelling the rotation confirmation dialog runs its
callback synchronously, but the dialog's widget closes in a task that
NativeWidgetAura::Close() posts to the current thread. The rotation
tests now use RunUntil() to wait until the dialog is gone. The accept
callback rotates the display synchronously in these tests: with no
wallpaper set, DisplayConfigurationController::SetDisplayRotation()
skips the animator and calls DisplayManager directly. In
GlobalAcceleratorsToggleAppList, the calls are deleted:
ProcessInController() reaches AppListControllerImpl::ToggleAppList(),
whose bubble Show() and Dismiss() update visibility synchronously, as
TestAppListClient runs the zero-state search callback inline.

[WebNN] Don't fuse DQ for logical ops with unsupported scale on LiteRT

LiteRT's quantized comparison kernel CHECK-fails if the input scale is
not finite and positive, or is exactly 1.0. WebNN allows any float
scale, so fusing the dequantize ops into a logical op could crash.
Skip the fusion in that case so the unfused dequantize ops handle it.

Ash: Make the security token session warning own its widget

This changelist is part of an ongoing series to move Ash widgets off
the deprecated NATIVE_WIDGET_OWNS_WIDGET and WIDGET_OWNS_NATIVE_WIDGET
ownership modes and onto CLIENT_OWNS_WIDGET, the mode views recommends
for all widgets. With it, the code that creates a widget owns it and
decides when it is destroyed. This removes a common source of dangling
pointers and window teardown bugs.

The security token session controller now owns the countdown warning's
widget instead of keeping a raw pointer to it, and destroys it once the
warning is no longer needed, even if the user closed the dialog first.

[ozone/wayland] Notify observers when a WaylandBubble is hidden

WaylandBubble notifies WaylandWindowObservers that it is configured when
it gets its wl_subsurface role in AddToParentAsSubsurface(), but not
when it loses the role in Hide(). XdgSurface notifies them in both
cases.

WaylandInputEmulate relies on this for ui_controls in tests: when a
window is configured, it attaches a test buffer and queues emulated
input until the frame callback of that buffer arrives, and it stops
waiting when the window is unconfigured. A bubble that is hidden right
after it is shown never gets the frame callback, so all emulated input
stays queued until the test times out.

This makes BrowserFocusTest.FocusTraversal time out on
linux-arm64-wayland-rel-fyi: focusing the location bar shows the WebUI
omnibox popup and hides it about 2 ms later, before the first Tab key
press is sent. It started when the popup moved to TopChromeWebUIProfile,
presumably because the popup renders sooner in the shared renderer
process, so it is shown before it is hidden.

Notify the observers in Hide() too, and re-enable the test on that
builder. With the builder's CI GN args, the test timed out 14 of 20
times without this.

[Bedrock] Migrate c/t:test_support (5/N) consumers: chrome_test_launcher

Add direct deps on previously-transitive targets and remove the
//c/t:test_support dep from //c/t/base:chrome_test_launcher. Part of
migrating //chrome/test:test_support's consumers to direct deps, in
preparation for deleting the test_support group.

chrome_test_launcher.h exposes chrome_main_delegate.h /
startup_timestamps.h (and, on Android, chrome_main_delegate_android.h);
these are provided by //chrome/app:test_support off-Android and
//chrome:chrome_android_core on Android, so they are public_deps.
in_process_browser_test (off-Android) / android_browser_test (Android)
and the win-only install_static test support are added as private deps
under the matching guards.

//chrome/app:test_support's visibility is limited to a small allowlist;
add //chrome/test/base:chrome_test_launcher to it since it now includes
chrome_main_delegate.h / the win crash reporter client header directly
(previously reached via //chrome/test:test_support).

Analysis/Plan: https://notes.nickdiego.dev/chromium/bedrocking-chrome-test

[browser_actuator] Populate chrome_major_version_number on upstream messages

The host needs the client Chrome major version for capability gating,
such as APC (crbug.com/553164475). Populate

`supported_features` stays empty and will follow separately.

Migrate ChromeSerialManager to JniRawPtr

Passing raw C++ pointers as primitive long values across JNI bypasses
type safety and lifetime checks.

Replace mNativePointer with
JniRawPtr<NativeSerialDeviceEnumeratorAndroid>, guard concurrent
executor callbacks against close(), and release the reference in
close().

Revert CHECK_EQ to DCHECK_EQ in Window::StackChildRelativeTo

In certain scenarios involving ARC overlay windows, child->parent()
might not equal this when StackChildRelativeTo is called. Revert the
CHECK_EQ conversion back to DCHECK_EQ to prevent crashes in release
builds while retaining debug assertions.

crash/84c529a888400000. Please see go/crash-autofix for more details.

[wtf] Enable HashTable modification checks by default

HashTable tracks container mutations with a modification counter and
verifies in iterator operations that the table is not modified during
iteration, previously only when DCHECK_IS_ON() is true. Add
enable_hash_table_modification_checks (enabled by default) and
enable_heap_hash_table_modification_checks (disabled by default) GN
build arguments so PartitionAlloc-backed HashTable instances enforce
CheckModifications() with CHECK_EQ() in release builds, matching Vector.
Also call RegisterModification() on both tables in HashTable::swap().

Store the counter as a uint32_t gated on kCheckModifications so 64-bit
sizeof(HashTable) is unchanged (fitting in trailing padding) and Oilpan
HeapHashTable pays no overhead while disabled. Mark HashTable iterators,
adapters, Modifications(), and RegisterModification() ALWAYS_INLINE so
CHECK_EQ() checks stay inline and LLVM SROA keeps iterators in registers
instead of spilling them to the stack in non-official release builds.

In InvalidationSet::InvalidatesElement(), check HasAttributes() before
element.hasAttributes() and invalidation_flags_.InvalidatesParts()
before element.HasPart() to avoid out-of-line NodeRareData lookups on
every element during style invalidation.

[WebNN] Emit identity for scalar pad to avoid empty paddings tensor on LiteRT

Padding a scalar (rank-0) input is a no-op, but SerializePad() still
built an empty [0, 2] paddings tensor for it. Some LiteRT delegates,
e.g. the ML Drift delegate, can't handle such a tensor and may
crash.

Serialize a scalar pad as an identity operation instead, reusing
SerializeIdentityOperation() as concat and reverse already do for their
no-op cases.

Make --disable-font-subpixel-positioning disable subpixel positioning

GetFontRenderParams() only skipped the block that computes subpixel
positioning from the device scale factor when the switch was present.
Since FontRenderParams::subpixel_positioning defaults to true and
Fontconfig never sets it, the switch actually enabled subpixel
positioning at 1x and kept Fontconfig's hinting at scale factors above
1x, the opposite of what its name says.

Compute subpixel rendering, subpixel positioning and hinting each in
one place, with subpixel positioning always set explicitly in a new
ShouldUseSubpixelPositioning() helper that returns false when the
switch is present. Hinting is still only overridden when antialiasing
is off or subpixel positioning is on, so the switch keeps the hinting
that Fontconfig requested.

signin: Pass callback to capabilities fetcher

AccountCapabilitiesFetcher stored a raw native callback pointer
allocated on the heap in C++ and passed across JNI as a long.

Pass a base::OnceCallback directly to the constructor wrapped as a Java
JniOnceCallback<AccountCapabilities> using JNI Zero's callback
conversion, and destroy any uninvoked callback when the native fetcher
is destroyed. This eliminates the raw pointer, the manual heap
allocation, and the static JNI callback method.

[variations] Honor --no-experiments in iOS about:flags startup

iOS ignores --no-experiments at startup. IOSChromeMainParts calls the
iOS ConvertFlagsToSwitches() and RegisterAllFeatureVariationParameters()
wrappers unconditionally, so about:flags entries still apply. Chrome's
about_flags::ConvertFlagsToSwitches() already returns early under the
switch, and variations::CreateFeatureList() skips both steps.

Make both iOS wrappers return early when --no-experiments is set, so
iOS already behaves like variations::CreateFeatureList() before it
migrates to it. ConvertFlagsToSwitches() checks the command line it is
given. RegisterAllFeatureVariationParameters() checks the process
command line and returns no variation IDs.

webui: Write resource bytes synchronously into Mojo data pipe

This CL writes in-memory WebUI resource bytes synchronously into a
payload-sized Mojo data pipe in `webui::GetPipe()`, falling back to the
default capacity and `mojo::DataPipeProducer` if allocation fails or the
payload exceeds the cap (2 MiB, or 512 KiB on ChromeOS and 32-bit). This
is guarded by `kWebUISyncDataPipeWrite` (disabled by default).

Previously, `webui::GetPipe()` always used a 64 KiB pipe and streamed
bytes asynchronously on a background thread-pool sequence (added in
crrev.com/c/7464900 before crrev.com/c/8353850 traced the pipe failures
to a shutdown broker race). Under startup contention, those extra hops
delayed WebUI resource delivery.

On `win-10-perf` Pinpoint (`browser-startup`, 46 bot-paired attempts),
`Startup.FirstWebContents.NonEmptyPaint3` improves by -21.0 ms (95% CI
[-54.0, -9.0] ms, 15/15 bots) and NTP FCP by -13.0 ms ([-59.0, -6.0]).
Linux and Mac (`N=400` each) are neutral to slightly favorable.

This change removes DidAddMessageToConsole and
ShouldReportDetailedMessageForSource from WebLocalFrameClient, as well
as DetailedConsoleMessageAdded from RenderFrameObserver.

Instead, console message notifications are now dispatched through
blink::WebLocalFrameObserver::DidAddMessageToConsole, and
ShouldReportDetailedMessageForSource is moved to blink::Platform.
Extensions and test runners are updated to observe WebLocalFrame
directly via WebLocalFrameObserver.

[WebNN] Fall back to LiteRT CPU when in-renderer WebGPU is unavailable

Previously, when `kWebNNLiteRTGpuInRenderer` routed `kGpu` requests to
`WebNNContextProviderInRenderer`, `CreateContextOnWorker` rejected them
with `kNotSupportedError` whenever `webgpu_properties` was invalid. On
build configurations without ML Drift WebGPU or Dawn (such as Android
and CastOS), or on systems where a WebGPU adapter/device cannot be
acquired at runtime (such as Linux X11 without Vulkan-GL interop,
software/blocklisted GPUs, or Android AAPM), `navigator.ml`
`createContext({deviceType: 'gpu'})` failed instead of falling back to
in-renderer CPU execution.

Keep routing `kGpu` requests to `WebNNContextProviderInRenderer` when
`kWebNNLiteRTGpuInRenderer` is enabled (so Android stays on the
in-renderer CPU fallback path rather than the GPU process), gate WebGPU
context initialization in `WebNNContextProviderInRenderer` on
`BUILDFLAG(BUILD_LITERT_WITH_ML_DRIFT) && BUILDFLAG(WEBNN_USE_DAWN)`,
and downgrade `options->device` to `mojom::Device::kCpu` when WebGPU is
unavailable at compile time or fails at runtime on the worker sequence.

[variations] Add shared CreateFeatureList startup component

Chrome and iOS run the same startup sequence to create
base::FeatureList, but ChromeFeatureListCreator and IOSChromeMainParts
currently duplicate that setup.

Add variations::CreateFeatureList() and FeatureListCreatorClient in
components/variations/feature_list_creator to share that sequence. Also
add shared network_time and variations startup helpers, and move
switches::kNoExperiments into components/webui/flags.

This CL introduces no production behavior changes yet. Chrome and iOS
migrate to the shared path in stacked follow-up CLs (combined end-state
reference: https://crrev.com/c/8561037/16).

Prevent duplicate TabStripModel observation in PCES

BrowserManagerService::AddBrowser registers a new browser in
ProfileBrowserCollection before notifying OnBrowserCreated observers
with ObserverListPolicy::ALL. If an earlier observer opens a startup tab
(such as BrowserRestoreObserver on ChromeOS) and lazily creates
PageContentExtractionService, PageContentExtractionTabStripModelObserver
attaches to the new browser via ForEach in its constructor before the
ongoing OnBrowserCreated loop notifies it. This causes a duplicate
TabStripModel::AddObserver call (triggering DUMP_WILL_BE_NOTREACHED
crash dumps) when opening a browser window.

This change tracks observed TabStripModel instances in
PageContentExtractionTabStripModelObserver and removes them in
OnTabStripModelDestroyed, skipping duplicate AddObserver calls in
OnBrowserCreated until BrowserCollection switches to EXISTING_ONLY
(crbug.com/431671320).

[Omnibox] Make the desktop AI Mode button stateful behind a flag

With OmniboxStatefulAiModeButton enabled on desktop, the AI Mode button
no longer disappears once AI Mode is entered:
- VISIBLE_ACTIVE (AI Mode, no text or attachments): the button stays
  visible; clicking it exits to conventional search standby with the
  original URL. As on desktop, this exits even with a custom tool
  active, unlike the delete button which first steps back to AI Mode.
- VISIBLE_SEND (AI Mode with text or attachments): clicking the button
  submits the query, the same way as the navigate button, which is
  hidden while the AI Mode button acts as the send button.
The AI Mode exit (delete) button is hidden in AI Mode, as the AI Mode
button replaces it. The state is derived from the request type and the
presence of text or attachments; it is never stored.

The keyboard selection preview of entering AI Mode, and the AI Mode
activation hint, are limited to conventional search. This needs no
flag check: without the flag, the button is hidden (so it can be
neither visible nor selected) outside conventional search.

The per-state accessibility labels, the activated styling and the send
arrow are added in follow-ups.

Revert "[Actor] Intercept JS dialogs during actuation"

This reverts commit 7abb7796b8ab20d39b005a31fa5a0debf477827e.

Reason for revert:
LUCI Bisection has identified this change as the culprit of a build failure. See the analysis: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/bisection/compile-analysis/b/8664827843880220305

Sample failed build: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8664827843880220305

If this is a false positive, please report it at http://b.corp.google.com/createIssue?component=1199205&description=Analysis%3A+https%3A%2F%2Fchromium-review.googlesource.com%2Fc%2Fchromium%2Fsrc%2F%2B%2F8812814&format=PLAIN&priority=P3&title=Wrongly+blamed+https%3A%2F%2Fci.chromium.org%2Fui%2Fp%2Fchromium%2Fbisection%2Fcompile-analysis%2Fb%2F8664827843880220305&type=BUG

Original change's description:
> [Actor] Intercept JS dialogs during actuation
>
> Previously, unhandled window.alert(), window.confirm(), and
> window.prompt() calls during actor actuation blocked the renderer on
> modal UI dialogs (or dropped the text in backgrounded/headless tabs),
> and isolated-world scripts could not intercept main-world dialogs such
> as those fired from async XHR or fetch callbacks.
>
> Add JavaScriptDialogInterceptor as a browser-layer
> JavaScriptDialogManager wired into the desktop, Android, and headless
> WebContentsDelegates while an active ActorTask controls a WebContents
> (guarded by the standalone kActorInterceptJavaScriptDialogs feature,
> disabled by default). Intercepted dialogs are synchronously resolved
> (alert accepted, confirm and prompt dismissed) without showing modal UI,
> recorded on ToolResultWithLatencyInfo::javascript_dialogs with type
> and dialog_message, and copied into the ExecuteJsResult proto's
> javascript_dialogs field in actions_data.proto. Entering actor control
> also dismisses any pre-existing tab-modal dialog so the renderer is not
> left frozen. Dialogs from opaque- or cross-origin subframes (e.g.
> sandboxed iframes) and non-MPArch guest WebContents (e.g.
> MimeHandlerViewGuest) are auto-dismissed without being recorded.
> beforeunload dialogs continue delegating to TabModalDialogManager on
> regular tabs (or auto-proceed on headless surfaces), and
> paused/user-controlled tabs continue delegating to
> TabModalDialogManager.
>
> BYPASS_LARGE_CHANGE_WARNING: Single cohesive JS dialog interception CL.

mac: End stale open mouse-down on mouse moved events

A nested event-tracking loop, such as the one AppKit runs for a native
<select> popup menu, can consume the left mouse-up, so the view where
the mouse-down started never sees it. That leaves two stale states:

- RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa's _hasOpenMouseDown stays set. While it is
  set, -shouldIgnoreMouseEvent: accepts moves over overlapping views.
  With DevTools docked, picking a value from a DevTools <select> (e.g.
  Sensors > Location) leaves the DevTools view handling moves over the
  inspected page, and the two views fight over the cursor: the page's
  cursor (e.g. pointer) flashes and reverts to an arrow until the user
  clicks inside DevTools.
- BaseView's _dragging stays set. While it is set, -mouseExited: holds
  back mouse exited events until the drag ends, which never happens.
  After closing a <select>, moving the mouse from the page to e.g. the
  bookmark bar then never sends the page a mouse leave, so a cursor
  (e.g. pointer) shown where the mouse left the page stays stuck.

AppKit only sends NSEventTypeMouseMoved while no mouse button is
pressed, so treat one as the end of any open mouse-down in
RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa, and of any drag in BaseView, which then sends
the mouse exited event it held back, if any. Rename
-[BaseView handleLeftMouseUp:] to -endDragWithEvent: to match. Drags are
unaffected because they arrive as NSEventType*MouseDragged.

[pip-ext] 20. Route standalone window events in WindowsEventRouter

In WindowsEventRouter::OnWindowControllerAdded(),
OnWindowControllerRemoved(), and OnWindowBoundsChanged(), check
WindowController::IsVisibleToTabsAPIForExtension() instead of requiring
a non-null BrowserWindowInterface, and use
WindowController::CreateWindowValueForExtension() in
OnWindowBoundsChanged(). This allows standalone WindowControllers (such
as Document Picture-in-Picture windows) to dispatch windows.onCreated,
windows.onBoundsChanged, and windows.onRemoved events while still
ignoring non-exposed controllers such as AppWindowController.

[metrics] Build and wire Structured Metrics on Android behind a flag

Enable structured_metrics_enabled (and debug internals) on Android and
wire StructuredMetricsService in ChromeMetricsServiceClient matching
Win/Mac/Linux, gated behind kChromeStructuredMetrics
(FEATURE_DISABLED_BY_DEFAULT on Android, enabled on bots via
fieldtrial_testing_config.json). This lets Gemini in Chrome (Glic)
record per-invocation structured metrics on Android;
https://crrev.com/c/8718709 adds background flushing.

With ChromeOS-only projects filtered and the validator refactored to
constexpr .rodata tables in the parent CL, the ~28 KB arm32 increase
comes from linking the core //components/metrics/structured runtime,
protos, the native chrome://metrics-internals/structured handler (the
WebUI itself ships in the DevUI DFM), the compact validator (~5.5 KB),
and Glic call sites.

Binary-Size: Size increase is unavoidable (see commit description).

Enable UseSCContentSharingPicker by default

Enable kUseSCContentSharingPicker by default on macOS and remove its
fieldtrial_testing_config.json entry ahead of rolling out to 100%
Stable, keeping the base::Feature guard as a kill switch.

Gate SCContentSharingPicker unconditionally on macOS 26.4+ across all
callsites via ShouldUseSCContentSharingPicker() in
desktop_media_picker_utils (inlined in native_screen_capture_picker.cc
due to //content layering):
- Earlier macOS versions have OS-level replayd issues and were excluded
  from the Stable rollout.
- Callsites previously checked inconsistent OS versions (14.0+, 15.0+,
  or none), which also caused CreatePlatformDependentVideoCaptureDevice
  to fail when NativeScreenCapturePickerMac was created on OS versions
  where the Chrome picker was still used.

WebView browser tests now that OOPIF PDF has launched everywhere.

The Kiosk AddingMimeHandlerGuestViewDoesNotCrash tests depended on
GuestView PDF, so they are removed. Add a TODO to restore coverage for
non-WebViewGuest guests with a non-PDF test.

Rename `exe_dir` to `src_dir` in `RunWebPageReplayCmd()` and remove
the duplicate `DIR_SRC_TEST_DATA_ROOT` lookup.

directory), but `exe_dir` held `base::DIR_SRC_TEST_DATA_ROOT` (the
source root).

Attribute navigations from extension script injection

A script injected with scripting.executeScript or tabs.executeScript can
navigate the tab, and those navigations were not attributed to the
extension. Set the extension actor when an extension injects a script,
the same way as for Runtime.evaluate.

The //extensions change only adds a no-op hook. Everything is gated by
Finch and enterprise policy.

Like Runtime.evaluate, any injected script tags the tab for now, which
is a known limitation.

ui/gl: Restore global GlWorkarounds in EGLInitializationDisplaysTest.DisableD3D11

EGLInitializationDisplaysTest.DisableD3D11 called gl::SetGlWorkarounds()
with disable_d3d11=true and never restored the global state at the end
of the test. When GLSurfaceEGLTest.FixedSizeExtension ran later in the
same test process on Windows, D3D11 initialization was skipped, leaving
zero EGL display types and crashing in GLSurfaceTestSupport.

Save and restore gl::GetGlWorkarounds() in DisableD3D11.

[updater] Skip inapplicable installer results cases before SetUp

Evaluate the per-test parameter skip predicates in
IntegrationInstallerResultsTest::SetUp() before calling
IntegrationTestMsi::SetUp(). On Windows x64, 121 of 171 parameterized
cases across TestCases, OnDemandTestCases, and RunMockOfflineMetaInstall
are inapplicable; skipping them before base fixture setup avoids 121
unnecessary IntegrationTest::SetUp(), ScopedServer, and MSI registry
cleanup cycles per system-scope run.

Skipping before ScopedServer creation also avoids hitting the
WSAESOCKTNOSUPPORT (10044) listen failure for those skipped cases when
they share a test batch process with
EventLoggerLifetimeTest.EventLoggerDoesNotRetainConfigurator (introduced
in crrev.com/c/8817690, tracked in crbug.com/587038399); cases that
actually run still require the root-cause fix. ScopedServer startup
failure handling is split into a follow-up CL.

https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium%3Aci/%3A%2F%2Fchrome%2Fupdater%5C%3Aupdater_tests_system%21gtest%3A%3AIntegrationInstallerResultsTest%23TestCases%2FIntegrationInstallerResultsTestCases.29?q=VHASH%3Aeee052c5ea679a71

user_manager: Skip redundant Local State commits on login

SaveUserOAuthStatus and SaveForceOnlineSignin unconditionally dirty
Local State via ScopedDictPrefUpdate and call CommitPendingWrite even
when the stored values already match.

Skip the update and CommitPendingWrite when the stored value in Local
State is unchanged to avoid redundant atomic writes and fdatasync calls
during existing-user ChromeOS logins.

[GEiC] Track the Glic provider the user knows they're on

The goal is to support notifying the user when their Glic provider was
switched between sessions, e.g. because an admin changed the
GeminiEnterpriseUrl policy. This CL adds the tracking; the notification
UI comes in a follow-up.

Adds glic.provider_switch_notice.known_provider_key, the provider the
user last onboarded to. A switch is reported when the latched provider
differs from it. When the user switches provider themselves (e.g. from
the relaunch prompt), it's cleared right before the restart, so that
switch isn't reported.

kGeicProviderSwitchNotice, disabled by default, controls whether a
switch is reported, and kGeic stays the overall kill switch. While
either is disabled, the known provider follows the latched one, so
enabling them later doesn't report an old switch.

[iOS][Passwords] Return page language in GetPageLanguage()

IOSChromePasswordManagerClient::GetPageLanguage() always returned an
empty language because of a TODO that said the client had no access
to the WebState. The client bridge now exposes the WebState, so use
the page's ChromeIOSTranslateClient and return the source language
from its TranslateManager's LanguageState, the same as desktop's
ChromePasswordManagerClient. Return an empty language if the
WebState, translate client or translate manager is missing.

Add unit tests for a WebState without a translate client, a page with
a detected source language, and a bridge without a WebState.

[TTC][HOTL] Report playback completion on dropped model audio

Follow-up from https://crrev.com/c/8760131 ([TTC][HOTL][5/X]).

When ConversationImpl routes captured microphone audio to a local HOTL
confirmation sink, it drops incoming model audio frames so the model
does not speak over the confirmation prompt. During review of CL
8760131, reviewers noted that dropping audio without notifying
PlaybackStatusReporter (https://crrev.com/c/8701282) hangs active model
turns.

Update ConversationImpl and Conversation documentation:
- In SetHotlAudioSink(), clear the playback queue and call
  PlaybackStatusReporter::CompleteIfNeeded() when activating a sink.
- In OnAudioOutput(), drop model audio while a sink is active or if
  playback completion was already reported, and complete the reporter
  immediately upon turn start if a sink is active.
- Update Conversation::SetHotlAudioSink() comments to match this
  contract and cover queue flushing, partial progress, and trailing chunk
  suppression in unit tests.
- Add TtcHotlProtocolBrowserTest in hotl_protocol_browsertest.cc
  verifying MES send/receive protocol flows for generation ending before
  vs after confirmation.

[shared-image] Use EndAccess() initialized state in EndAccessDawn()

D3DImageBacking::EndAccessDawn() previously queried
dawn::native::IsTextureSubresourceInitialized() and called SetCleared()
before acquiring the backing lock or calling
SharedTextureMemory::EndAccess(). When Queue::WriteTexture() records a
copy into Dawn's passive pending command context and Device::Destroy()
discards those commands before DissociateMailbox(), Dawn's CPU-side
subresource initialized bit stays set even though the GPU copy never
executes and SharedTextureMemory::EndAccess() reports
initialized=false. Reading IsTextureSubresourceInitialized() directly
therefore marked an unwritten D3D11 texture as cleared.

Update D3DImageBacking::EndAccessDawn() to promote the cleared state via
SetClearedInternal() from SharedTextureMemoryEndAccessState::initialized
after SharedTextureMemory::EndAccess(), and log an error if EndAccess()
fails. Move the direct IsTextureSubresourceInitialized() check (using
SetClearedInternal() under the backing lock) into the persistent
Graphite Dawn access branch, which keeps access open and skips
EndAccess().

Also add CreateSharedImage() and CreateDawnD3D12Device() helpers in
D3DImageBackingFactoryTest alongside a regression test covering
Queue::WriteTexture() followed by Device::Destroy() before ending Dawn
access. Note that a follow-up CL migrates existing tests to these
helpers; keeping that cleanup separate makes this fix easier to merge.

parent
713643630fe8f57200cc3616d3dcc680e874259c [ diff ] 
[BreakoutBox] close frames that cannot be enqueued after stream teardown

Frames popped from the FrameQueue are wrapped in WebCodecs objects and
enqueued into the readable stream in a separate posted task. If the
stream is closed in the meantime (track stopped or stream cancelled),
the controller silently drops the chunk, leaving the frame to be
garbage collected without close(). Besides reporting an unclosed-frame
warning even when the application closes every frame it reads, the
unclosed frame keeps its capture buffer pool slot reserved until GC
runs, which can stall delivery of new frames.

Check ReadableStreamDefaultController::CanCloseOrEnqueue() before
enqueueing, and close() the frame immediately when it can no longer be
delivered.

[Actor] Don't wait for focus to reauth on headless pages

A headless actor page has no tab, so the user can't focus it.
ChromeActorLoginDelegateClient::IsTaskInFocus() CHECKed for a tab, and
AttemptLoginTool waited for the tab to be focused before retrying a
login that needs device reauth.

IsTaskInFocus() now returns false for a page without a tab, and
AttemptLoginTool replies kLoginDeviceReauthRequired for a headless page
instead of waiting for focus.

A tab demoted to a headless page while waiting for focus is left to a
follow-up that tells tasks about demotion.

NO_IFTTT=Comment-only change

[FacilitatedPayments] Only swap bottom sheet screens when one is showing

FacilitatedPaymentsPaymentMethodsView.setVisible(true) treats
BottomSheetController.isSheetOpen() as "this view is showing a screen"
and swaps mCurrentScreen for mNextScreen. isSheetOpen() is true whenever
any content is open, including another feature's sheet or this view's
own sheet still animating closed after mCurrentScreen was cleared. In
those cases mCurrentScreen is null and the swap throws a
NullPointerException. The assert guarding it only fires on Canary.

Require an active non-hiding screen before swapping. When this view is
still animating closed, report SCREEN_COULD_NOT_BE_SHOWN instead of
no-oping requestShowContent(this, true), and ignore onSheetClosed
events for other sheet contents.

Record Glic{GlicProvider}.Fre.Android.SelectionOutcome at Android
invocation routing for unconsented profiles, and

Clear LobsterCandidateStore on query change and UI close

LobsterCandidateStore kept every generated candidate in an unbounded
map, and LobsterController::active_session_ retained the store after
the Lobster bubble closed.

The Lobster UI replaces all displayed candidates when the query
changes and only appends more for the same query. Clear the store when
RequestCandidates() is called with a different query, when the UI
closes via CloseUI, CommitAsInsert, CommitAsDownload, or bubble
dismissal, and ignore in-flight responses for superseded queries or
after UI close.

kinds of reasons.

[ContextHub] Add SearchQuery source references to Auto Todos.

CMS can now cite Search History queries (SourceReference.search_query,
synced in the parent CL) for LaunchPad todos. Thread the new reference
type through the browser, mirroring ChromeHistoryEntry:

- Add context_hub::SearchQuery (query, timestamp) to the
  SourceReference variant and a matching SearchQuery struct/union
  member in context_hub.mojom, with StructTraits/UnionTraits for both
  the entry variant and the CMS proto.
- Convert search_query references in both directions in
  ContextHubService (CMS response -> AutoTodoEntry, and existing todos
  -> dedup request). Queries are trimmed and blank ones are dropped
  when parsing the CMS response.
- Build the search URL browser-side: ContextHubService asks
  TemplateURLService for the default search provider and only surfaces
  a Search History reference when that provider is Google, generating
  SearchQuery.search_url from its template. References that cannot be
  given a URL are dropped. The WebUI consumes search_url as-is and
  never constructs a search URL itself.

The WebUI does not render search query references yet; that follows in
a separate CL. Until then todo-item simply shows no link for them.

Add Dawn Windows/Software testers

Adds two new Dawn CI testers for testing Windows/x64 with software
renderers (both ToT and DEPS) and adds them to the corresponding trybot
mirrors. These testers do not currently run any tests, but will run the
web tests using SwiftShader in the future.

"Software" is chosen over "SwiftShader" since SwiftShader is on its way
out and using a generic name allows us to avoid renaming the testers in
the future. Similarly, "Win" is chosen over the historical "Win10" since
these are liable to switch to Windows 11 at some point.

[WebNN] Replace PACKAGE_VERSION with webnn::PackageVersion

execution_providers_info.h included <appmodel.h> only for
PACKAGE_VERSION. <appmodel.h> isn't self-contained: it uses UINT32,
PWSTR, etc. from <windows.h>, so a file that included this header
without <windows.h> first failed with "unknown type name 'UINT32'".

Add webnn::PackageVersion, a plain struct of four uint16_t whose
defaulted comparisons replace the hand-written operator<, and use it
in place of PACKAGE_VERSION, including the mojo typemap. It is
converted to PACKAGE_VERSION only where it is passed to the Windows
package dependency API.

This removes the <appmodel.h> dependency from
execution_providers_info.h, win_app_runtime_package_info.h,
platform_functions_ort.h and the mojo traits, so they no longer rely
on <windows.h> being included first.

[Capture] Use getDisplayMedia in TabCapturePerformanceTest

TabCapturePerformanceTest starts capture through a test extension that
calls chrome.tabCapture. It is disabled on Linux, Mac, and ChromeOS
because it flakes and reports a bogus 100% capture fail rate. Most
capture goes through getDisplayMedia(), and the extension only changes
how capture starts, not the compositor-to-renderer path under test.

Start capture from the test page with getDisplayMedia() and
preferCurrentTab, and move the test to chrome/browser/media/webrtc.
Merge the base class into the test, delete the extension, and move
balls.html to chrome/test/data/webrtc. Skip the test on MemorySanitizer
and on bots without a hardware GPU, and drop the software compositing
and WebRTC loopback variants.

Hold the BEST_EFFORT fence only during tracing, wait for the receiver
video to play before tracing, and accept the result=kSuccess trace
argument.

Bypass-Check-License: Moved from extensions/api/tab_capture

WebNN: Accept constant-folded EPContext models with no nodes

When the Compiler process compiles a graph whose outputs depend only on
constants, ORT's constant folding runs before graph partitioning and
evaluates every node with CPU kernels, replacing the graph with
initializers. The execution provider then has nothing to compile, so the
compiled model contains no nodes and no EPContext node.

The GPU process's EPContext model validator required exactly one
EPContext node and reported such models as bad messages. This breaks,
for example, single-op WPT cases whose inputs are all constants on the
OpenVINO NPU execution provider.

Relax the check to at most one EPContext node. A model with no nodes
creates no kernels in the GPU process; ORT only copies the initializers
to the outputs. Non-EPContext nodes and multiple nodes are still
rejected, and graph optimizations stay disabled in the GPU process.

Update SECURITY.md, the histogram summary and related comments to
describe the zero-node case.

Skip DOMActivate when there are no listeners for it

Node::DefaultEventHandler() dispatches a DOMActivate event for each
click that isn't handled before it, e.g. on buttons, which creates a
UIEvent and its event path. Since CleanUpActivationBehavior, no default
event handler handles DOMActivate, so only its listeners can observe
it.

Add DOMActivate to the listener types of Document, and don't dispatch
it if the document has no listener for it. Guarded by the
SkipDOMActivateWithoutListeners kill switch, which depends on
CleanUpActivationBehavior.

No behavior change.
